definition: Training embeddings so meaningful information concentrates in the leading dimensions, letting one model serve multiple sizes (truncate 1024-dim vectors to 256 with modest loss).
details: Training embeddings so meaningful information concentrates in the leading dimensions, letting one model serve multiple sizes (truncate 1024-dim vectors to 256 with modest loss). Cuts storage and search cost with one model.

explainer.lead: Matryoshka Representation Learning trains embeddings so meaningful information concentrates in the leading dimensions, letting one model serve several sizes. It matters because a single model can cut storage and search cost.

tiers.eli5: Like nesting dolls, the important part of the embedding is packed into the first few numbers, so you can keep just the outer layers and still get most of the meaning.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train once, then truncate, for example 1024-dimension vectors down to 256, accepting modest loss. The pitfall is assuming truncation to any size is nearly free — the loss is modest, not zero.
tiers.paperLevel: Information is trained to concentrate in the leading dimensions so that truncated vectors remain usable; one model serves multiple embedding sizes.

explainer.example: A search index stores 1024-dimension embeddings and serves a cheaper 256-dimension index by truncating the same vectors, with modest quality loss.
